claims.claim_text: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model that powers its AI chip design platform.
claims.excerpt: Today, we release Ripple-65B Preview, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model that powers our AI chip design platform.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says Ripple-65B Preview was pretrained on 12 trillion tokens and supports up to 1M context length.
claims.excerpt: The model is pretrained on 12 trillion tokens with support for up to 1M context length.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says Ripple-65B Preview scored 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, a U.S. open-weight state of the art, ahead of Reflection Beam 501B (80.1), Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4), Thinking Machines Inkling 975B (63.8) and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B (56.4).
claims.excerpt: achieving U.S. open-weight state-of-the-art (80.52) on TerminalBench 2.1 and surpassing significantly larger US open-weight models such as Reflection Beam 501B (80.1), Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4)

claims.claim_text: Ripple-65B Preview is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, OpenRouter and Fireworks.
claims.excerpt: Ripple-65B Preview is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, OpenRouter, and Fireworks.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says it developed and trained Ripple-65B Preview for only $32M in full R&D cost, about one-tenth the estimated cost of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding.
claims.excerpt: we developed and trained Ripple-65B Preview for only $32M, which is one-tenth the cost of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding, as estimated to the best of our knowledge.¹

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says its $32M figure covers all R&D from scratch, including ladder development, data mixing, evals, debugging, synthetic data generation, posttraining recipe development and the final pretraining and posttraining run.
claims.excerpt: Note that $32M is our full R&D cost starting from scratch, including pretraining ladder development, data mixing, evals, debugging, synthetic data generation, posttraining recipe development, and the final hero pretraining and posttraining run.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says it reached a TerminalBench 2.1 score of 80.5 with only 1.4M rollouts, roughly 70x fewer than Reflection Beam, the prior SOTA.
claims.excerpt: We reached a TerminalBench 2.1 score of 80.5 with only 1.4M rollouts, roughly 70x fewer rollouts than Reflection Beam, the prior SOTA.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says Ripple-65B Preview is a dense Transformer rather than a Mixture-of-Experts model, and it maintained about 40% MFU through pretraining and posttraining with simple sharding, no custom kernels and no quantization.
claims.excerpt: we chose to train a modernized dense Transformer model rather than use Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) like other labs.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says its model ladder changes improved compute efficiency on code (dolma_stack CE) by up to 16x at 4B scale versus the Olmo 3 ladder.
claims.excerpt: the compounded changes improved compute efficiency on code as measured by dolma_stack CE by up to 16x at 4B model scale.

claims.claim_text: Ricursive says the model's small parameter size lets it run efficiently on local devices such as NVIDIA DGX Spark.
claims.excerpt: The model’s small parameter envelope also enables it to run efficiently on local devices such as NVIDIA DGX Spark
